description: Alkaline hydrolysis of ethyl ethanoate: first order in ester and in hydroxide, so second order overall. Hydroxide is used up as acetate forms, so the pH falls as the reaction goes; with equal starting concentrations 1/[OH⁻] rises linearly with time, with slope k.

references: k ≈ 0.11 L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 25 °C and Ea ≈ 40–48 kJ/mol are typical literature values for ethyl acetate saponification

description: Ethanol–water at 1 atm: the vapour is richer in ethanol than the liquid it boils from, up to the azeotrope near x = 0.894 (about 95.6 % by mass), beyond which distillation cannot enrich it.

references: Ethanol–water vapour–liquid equilibrium at 101.3 kPa, as tabulated in standard chemical engineering handbooks

description: Orthophosphate and molybdate form phosphomolybdate in acid; ascorbic acid reduces it to the blue. With the reagent in excess the blue forms first order in phosphate, half in about 4 minutes at 21 °C: 20 minutes is full colour. No ascorbic acid, no blue.

references: Murphy and Riley (1962), the ascorbic-acid molybdenum-blue method

description: Zinc dust reduces nitrate to nitrite where the liquid touches it: a few per cent a minute with a drop of slurry in 5 mL, so standards and samples must have the same time on the zinc. Once the dust settles and the liquid is taken off it, reduction stops.

provenance.notes: Teaching-scale rate chosen for a minute's partial reduction; over-reduction past nitrite is not modelled.

description: Nitrite diazotises sulfanilamide, which couples with NED to a magenta azo dye (λmax 540 nm). With the reagent in excess the colour is half formed in about 3 minutes.

references: Griess reaction: diazotisation of sulfanilamide and coupling with N-(1-naphthyl)ethylenediamine

description: Base hydrolysis of 4-nitrophenyl benzoate: first order in ester and in hydroxide (k = 0.6 M⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 21 °C). With hydroxide in excess it is pseudo-first order, kobs = k[OH⁻]; the 4-nitrophenolate released is yellow (405 nm).

references: Hammett: log(k/k0) = rho sigma with rho = 2.0 and k0 = 0.6 M⁻¹ s⁻¹ (illustrative values of the right order for aryl benzoates in aqueous acetone)

description: Fischer esterification of 4-nitrocinnamic acid with ethanol, catalysed by sulfuric acid: first order in the acid, in ethanol and in the catalyst. Slow at room temperature (about fifty times slower than at reflux); reversible, so water drives it back (see the hydrolysis).

references: Fischer–Speier esterification: acid-catalysed, reversible, K about 4 for simple acids with ethanol
Rate constant illustrative: of the order that gives most of the ester in an hour's reflux in ethanol with about 1 mL of concentrated H2SO4 per 20 mL

description: The reverse of the Fischer esterification: acid-catalysed hydrolysis of ethyl 4-nitrocinnamate. With the forward reaction it sets K = [ester][water]/([acid][ethanol]) = 4, so excess ethanol and little water push the equilibrium towards the ester.

references: K = 4 (ethyl acetate's esterification equilibrium, taken for this ester)

description: 4-Nitrophenol acylated by benzoyl chloride with triethylamine as the base: first order in each (k = 6.0 M⁻² s⁻¹ at 0 °C), so it is over within minutes in the cold. Exothermic in fact; the heat is not modelled.

references: Hammett rho 1.5 for aroyl chlorides acylating a phenoxide (illustrative; k0 = 6 M⁻² s⁻¹ at 0 °C)

description: Water turns benzoyl chloride into the acid and HCl: first order in each (k = 7 × 10⁻⁴ M⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 25 °C, so a half-life of about 20 s in water but hours in dried THF).

references: Benzoyl chloride in water: half-life of the order of 15-20 s at 25 °C

description: Acid decomposes thiosulfate into colloidal sulfur (which clouds the liquid) and sulfur dioxide: S₂O₃²⁻ + 2H⁺ → S + SO₂ + H₂O. First order in each, so the time for the same cloudiness halves when either is doubled; it roughly doubles in speed for every 10 °C.

provenance.notes: Rate constant calibrated to the classroom timings (0.15 M thiosulfate with 2 M acid: the cross goes in about half a minute at 20 °C); Ea of the right order.

description: S₂O₈²⁻ + 2I⁻ → 2SO₄²⁻ + I₂, first order in each (the iodine clock). Thiosulfate in the mixture turns the iodine straight back into iodide until it is used up; then free iodine turns the starch blue-black.

references: k ≈ 0.011 dm³ mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 25 °C, Ea about 50–55 kJ/mol (classic clock-reaction data)

description: Bromine adds across the C=C double bond of an alkene at once, so bromine water is decolourised when shaken with it; an alkane does not react.

provenance.notes: Rate illustrative, calibrated to classroom timings.

description: Acidified dichromate oxidises a primary alcohol to an aldehyde, turning from orange to green chromium(III). Dichromate counts as its chromium(VI) (two per dichromate); the rate goes as [H⁺].

provenance.notes: Rate illustrative, calibrated to classroom timings.

description: Acidified dichromate oxidises a secondary alcohol to a ketone, turning green. Dichromate counts as its chromium(VI) (two per dichromate); the rate goes as [H⁺].

provenance.notes: Rate illustrative, calibrated to classroom timings.

description: Acidified dichromate oxidises methanol, turning green. Dichromate counts as its chromium(VI) (two per dichromate); the rate goes as [H⁺].

provenance.notes: Rate illustrative, calibrated to classroom timings.

description: An aldehyde is oxidised to a carboxylic acid by acidified dichromate (a ketone is not). Dichromate counts as its chromium(VI) (two per dichromate); the rate goes as [H⁺].

provenance.notes: Rate illustrative, calibrated to classroom timings.

description: An aldehyde reduces the silver(I) of Tollens’ reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) to metallic silver within minutes at room temperature, faster when warm: a silver mirror. Ketones do not.

provenance.notes: Rate illustrative, calibrated to classroom timings.

description: An aldehyde reduces the complexed copper(II) of Fehling’s or Benedict’s solution to red copper(I) oxide when heated in alkali. Ketones do not.

provenance.notes: Rate illustrative, calibrated to classroom timings.

description: Iodine in alkali oxidises ethanol to ethanal, then triiodinates its CH₃CO– group and cleaves it: yellow iodoform.

provenance.notes: Rate illustrative, calibrated to classroom timings.

description: Propan-2-ol, oxidised to propanone, gives iodoform.

provenance.notes: Rate illustrative, calibrated to classroom timings.

description: Propanone (CH₃CO–) gives iodoform with iodine in alkali.

provenance.notes: Rate illustrative, calibrated to classroom timings.

description: Ethanal, the only aldehyde with CH₃CO–, gives iodoform.

provenance.notes: Rate illustrative, calibrated to classroom timings.

description: Phenols give a violet complex with neutral iron(III) chloride; alcohols do not.

provenance.notes: Rate illustrative, calibrated to classroom timings.
